subject: Proposal: Tiered Monthly Commits with Seasonal Buffer and Launch Decelerator
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@orbitanalytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Aug 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Tiered Monthly Commits with Seasonal Buffer and Launch Decelerator

Hi Elaine / Ryan —

Thanks again for the call earlier. As discussed, attached is a concise proposal that balances OrbitAnalytics' need for headroom during your November product launch with predictable unit economics for both teams. Key ideas below; full details in the attached SOW and the usage forecast CSV.

Summary (high level):
- Monthly committed tokens on a 3-month staircase: base -> step-up -> peak, aligned to your rollout calendar.
- Per-token discount tiers applied to the committed bucket (5%, 12%, 18% at 500M, 1.5B, 3B committed monthly averages).
- Seasonal buffer: a temporary 20% capacity cushion for launch months (Nov–Dec) that doesn't immediately change pricing tiers (protects latency/availability).
- Launch decelerator: if actual utilization falls >35% below committed volume for two consecutive months after launch, we provide a one-time rollback mechanism that scales committed level down with a pro-rated true-up to the prior quarter.

Questions for Orbit: please confirm the month-by-month throughput expectation (attached CSV) and whether you prefer a monthly true-up or quarterly true-up at the end of each billing quarter. Also: any procurement timing constraints we should bake into the SOW sign date?

Next steps I propose:
1) Orbit to confirm forecast + preferred true-up cadence by Aug 4.
2) Redwood to turn SOW into a DocuSign-ready draft by Aug 6.
3) Small canary rollout terms (no discount change) for Sep to validate traffic shaping.

Attachments: Orbit_Usage_Forecast_Aug2025.csv (sample month granularity), SOW_Orbit_v2.pdf (commercial terms).

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: Elaine Park <elaine@orbitanalytics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Ryan Cho <ryan@orbitanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Aug 2025 14:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Tiered Monthly Commits with Seasonal Buffer and Launch Decelerator

Thanks Rachel — this looks thoughtful and close to what we discussed. A couple of clarifying items before we prep legal: 

1) The discount ladder: can you confirm whether the discount percentage applies only to committed volume tiers or to all consumption once a tier is hit? For our models we prefer discount to apply to the committed bucket only, with overage priced at a fixed (non-discounted) per-token rate.
2) The "launch decelerator" sounds reasonable, but can the rollback be limited to a single step (e.g., reduce to prior tier rather than re-baselining monthly)? We are concerned about unpredictability for forecasting.
3) True-up cadence: we'd like monthly true-ups if possible — helps accounting and cash-flow. That said, we want a soft cushion the first two months post-launch so the true-up ignores up to 10% shortfall.

We can confirm the forecast attached is accurate (added a few lines to the CSV). Procurement has a PO submission target of Sep 12.

On item 1 and 2, happy to take whatever language keeps both sides comfortable.

Thanks — Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Platform Engineering, OrbitAnalytics
elaine@orbitanalytics.com | (212) 555-0198

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Elaine Park <elaine@orbitanalytics.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Tiered Monthly Commits with Seasonal Buffer and Launch Decelerator

Elaine — good questions. A few clarifications from commercial/pricing: 

- Discount application: Our standard structure is that the committed bucket receives the discounted rate; any consumption beyond the committed amount is billed at the published overage rate (no retroactive discount on overage). That matches your preference and keeps invoicing predictable.
- Decelerator rollback: we can limit rollback to "one tier down" for the first eligible rollback event, subject to a pro-rata true-up for the period being reduced. If a second consecutive shortfall occurs, we can revisit with a capped re-baseline (not a full immediate reduction to base).
- True-up cadence: Redwood supports monthly true-ups. For launch months we can apply the 10% grace on shortfall for the first two months post-launch (Nov/Dec) as requested.

Operational notes: snapshot for committed usage will be taken at UTC midnight on the final day of each month. Invoices reflect committed vs actual for the month with true-up adjustments the following invoice.

If those sound acceptable we will update the SOW language to reflect: committed-discount-only, overage-rate, one-tier decelerator cap, monthly true-up with two-month launch grace.

-Rishi
Head of Pricing | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: Elaine Park <elaine@orbitanalytics.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Ryan Cho <ryan@orbitanalytics.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Aug 2025 09:11:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Tiered Monthly Commits with Seasonal Buffer and Launch Decelerator

Thanks Rishi — that mapping addresses our main concerns. A couple of small asks before we sign: 

- Can you include a short clause that allows a one-time emergency cap reduction if our launch is delayed >60 days due to extenuating circumstances (requires mutual written agreement)?
- For reporting: we need a daily token usage CSV export for our finance and SRE teams during the two launch months. Is that something Redwood can provide via the console or S3 push?

Procurement note: we'll aim for PO submission by Sep 12 but legal will need SOW finalized to start their review.

—Elaine

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>

Elaine / Ryan — great, glad we're converging. Action items from Redwood side: 

- We'll add the one-time emergency cap reduction clause (requires written mutual agreement) to the SOW.
- Karthik will enable daily token usage exports and provide S3 push instructions; Neha will confirm retention and CSV schema. Expect an export readiness note in the SOW.
- Legal/commercial: Rishi and Priyom will push an updated, DocuSign-ready SOW by Aug 6 EOD PT.

Rachel attaching the updated forecast and a draft SOW in this thread for your legal team to review. If PO timing holds (Sep 12) we can target service start Oct 1 with a small Sep canary to validate traffic shaping.

Attachments: Orbit_Usage_Forecast_Aug2025.csv, SOW_Orbit_v2.pdf

Talk soon —
